report.summary: Analyzed daedalus/structcore/topology.py (chunk 1/1): module provides spectral graph cut analysis of import graph. 1 public function, 3 private functions, 2 constants, 1 module-level variable. All claims checked against code.
risks: spectral_partition | medium | The function returns partition_values with 1.0 or -1.0 based on side_a membership, but for disconnected graph it uses _balanced_component_cut which assigns whole components; the values are consistent but may not reflect eigenvector sign. | Check if callers expect partition_values to correspond to eigenvector sign; if so, this is intentional fallback.

_sweep_cut | low | The function uses nx.cut_size to compute cut edges after determining split point; but during the sweep it also maintains cut_edges variable which may not match nx.cut_size if graph is modified (not modified here). | Verify that cut_edges from sweep and nx.cut_size give same result; if not, which one is correct?

handoff.purpose: Provide spectral analysis (Fiedler vector, sweep cut) of structural import graph for visualization, with explicit caveats.

symbols.name: HAVE_MATH
symbols.note: Boolean flag indicating whether optional dependencies (networkx, numpy, scipy) are available.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_MAX_NODES
symbols.note: Default maximum number of nodes for spectral partition; set to 10,000.

symbols.name: _empty
symbols.note: Private helper returning a dict indicating analysis unavailable, with reason and optional node/edge counts.

symbols.name: _balanced_component_cut
symbols.note: Private function assigning whole disconnected components to two roughly balanced sides.

symbols.name: _sweep_cut
symbols.note: Private function performing sweep cut along Fiedler ordering to find best conductance partition.

symbols.name: spectral_partition
symbols.note: Public function analyzing import graph and returning two-way visualization cut with spectral method, including fallbacks for small graphs, disconnected graphs, and unavailable dependencies.

claims.text: Optional, read-only spectral analysis of the structural import graph.
claims.why: The module provides spectral_partition function which performs spectral analysis and returns results; it is read-only (no side effects).

claims.text: This module is an analysis/visualization aid.  A low graph cut does *not* establish independent edit scopes, semantic ownership, or conflict-free Git branches, so callers must never treat its partitions as a write-safety proof.
claims.why: The docstring explicitly warns against using cut for write-safety; the code returns partitions with reason strings emphasizing analysis-only purpose.

claims.text: Assign whole disconnected components to two roughly balanced sides.
claims.why: The function sorts components by size and assigns each to the side with smaller total size, achieving roughly balanced partition.

claims.text: Choose the best conductance cut along the Fiedler ordering.
claims.why: The function iterates over ordered nodes, computes conductance for each prefix, and selects the best according to (conductance, balance).

claims.text: A sweep cut is more stable than splitting solely on the arbitrary sign of an eigenvector and avoids pathological one-node partitions when possible.
claims.why: The function uses min_partition_fraction to enforce minimum partition size, avoiding one-node partitions; it evaluates all valid splits, not just sign-based split.

claims.text: ``idx`` lets API callers reuse the exact project-scoped structural index (including ``center`` and ``ignore`` rules).
claims.why: The code uses idx if provided, but the content of idx (center, ignore rules) is not defined in this chunk; it comes from index module.

claims.text: The computation uses a sparse normalized Laplacian; it deliberately refuses oversized graphs instead of allocating the dense ``N x N`` matrix used by the prototype.
claims.why: The code builds a sparse Laplacian via nx.normalized_laplacian_matrix; it returns early with error if node count exceeds max_nodes.
The _empty call provides this message when HAVE_MATH is False.

claims.text: a one-node graph has no Fiedler vector
claims.why: For single node, the function returns method 'singleton' with reason 'a one-node graph has no Fiedler vector'.

claims.text: the graph is disconnected; no unique Fiedler vector exists, so whole components were balanced without cutting edges
claims.why: When component_count > 1, the function returns method 'connected_components' with that reason; it uses _balanced_component_cut and sets cut_edges=0.

claims.text: A disconnected graph has one zero eigenvalue per component.  Do not fabricate the uncomputed remainder of the spectrum.
claims.why: The code sets eigenvalues to [0.0] * min(component_count, 8), which gives one zero per component up to 8, and does not compute more.

claims.text: analysis-only graph cut; it does not prove semantic independence or conflict-free edit scopes
claims.why: The method 'normalized_laplacian_sweep' includes this reason in the returned dict.

observations.what: The module uses 'math' extra name but the docstring says 'install the math extra'; the import tries networkx, numpy, scipy but not a package named 'math'.
For empty graph (no nodes), the function returns _empty with reason 'the structural import graph is empty' but node_count=0, edge_count not set explicitly; _empty defaults to 0 for both.

The function _sweep_cut uses nx.cut_size to compute cut after split, but during sweep it maintains cut_edges variable; both should agree but there is potential inconsistency if graph changes (not happening here).
For disconnected graph, partition_values are set to 1.0 or -1.0 based on side_a membership, but these do not come from eigenvector signs; this is a fallback.
